_comment: User-supplied benchmark config, consumed by sweep_bench.py (the InferencePerfAnalyzer-driven pytest sweep). Everything here is gathered from the user's request. Copy to bench_config.json and edit. See SKILL.md 'Gathering the config'.
_gpu_count: physical GPUs on the node (e.g. 8 for p5.48xlarge / g6e.48xlarge). Every sharding's tp*dp MUST equal gpu_count so each run occupies the whole box (fair per-instance comparison).
_image: ONE image for ALL regimes (engine-matched comparison). docker transport: pulled by setup.sh. kaizen transport: the BAKED image (IPA+pytest pre-installed) — pass it as KAIZEN_IMAGE in the workload command; this field is then informational.
_docker_env: extra env for the vLLM server container, docker transport ONLY (e.g. {"TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST":"10.0"} for Blackwell, or a FlashInfer-MoE toggle). Under the kaizen transport, set env in the workload command instead (the pod IS the server). Read by IPA's server_handle_pool as this module's DOCKER_ENV.

_hf_id_by_regime_example.fp8: <point the fp8 regimes at a pre-quantized FP8 checkpoint, e.g. neuralmagic/…-FP8>

_models: models to benchmark. key = short label (output-dir prefix), hf_id = exact HF id (the BASE, usually bf16, checkpoint). Optional per-model overrides: 'shardings' / 'concurrencies' (e.g. a big model that only fits at high TP — SEE 'Sizing for large / MoE models' in SKILL.md and PRUNE non-fitting shardings up front; a sharding that OOMs on server start is skipped but still costs a start attempt), 'regimes' (list of regime NAMES to restrict this model to — e.g. skip fp8 regimes for a model with no quantized checkpoint), 'hf_id_by_regime' ({regime_name: checkpoint} to point a regime at a pre-quantized HF checkpoint), 'moe' (true → adds --enable-expert-parallel; REQUIRED for MoE models like Mixtral / Qwen3-235B / gpt-oss), and 'rope_scaling' ({...} → --rope-scaling for shapes whose max-model-len exceeds the model's native context window; needed e.g. to run a 32K shape on a model with a smaller native window). NOTE: shardings are keyed per-MODEL not per-regime — if the fitting shardings differ by precision (bf16 fits fewer TP than fp8), express each precision as its OWN model entry (same hf_id / an fp8 hf_id, restricted via 'regimes' + its own 'shardings').

regimes.name: fp8
regimes._hint: FP8 weights via a pre-quantized checkpoint (set models[].hf_id_by_regime.fp8) OR online quant (add "quantization": "fp8"); kv_cache_dtype fp8 = FP8 KV. Weights, KV, and attention-backend are INDEPENDENT — record which actually engaged.

_regimes: the REGIME axis: precision/quantization x speculative-decoding, swept in ONE run. name = label (becomes regime_key in the deliverables); prec = precision label for grouping (bf16/fp8/awq/…); optional per-regime kv_cache_dtype, quantization (online weight quant), speculative (passed verbatim as vLLM --speculative-config; e.g. {"method":"eagle","model":"<draft hf id>","num_speculative_tokens":3}), extra_flags. ALL regimes run on the SAME 'image' above, so spec-vs-nospec and quant-vs-bf16 are ENGINE-MATCHED (the fix for the classic 'spec ran on a different vLLM build' pitfall). Omit this whole block for a single bf16 no-spec regime. QUANTIZED WEIGHTS are usually a checkpoint swap: set models[].hf_id_by_regime.<name> to a pre-quantized HF checkpoint (vLLM auto-detects the method — no flag needed).
_shapes: input/output token shapes per request (one sweep per shape). THE TWO MILESTONE STANDARD SHAPES (Neuron Agentic Optimization: Performance Milestones, Table 1) are 8192/1024 (8:1, SemiAnalysis InferenceX v2 default — agentic/multi-turn) and 32768/2048 (16:1 — large agentic coding, the KV-cache-pressure regime not visible at 8k). 512/1 is a CHEAP SMOKE point only, NOT a milestone shape. Keep IDENTICAL to the Neuron run (neuron_bench_config.example.json) for a valid comparison; milestone comparisons use dataset=random + random_range_ratio 0.0 (EXACT shapes) so both platforms see the same lengths (Neuron pads to compiled buckets, so only exact shapes are comparable). For a one-off non-milestone study, other shapes (2K/128, 4K/256, etc.) can be substituted per profiling-targets.md.
_shardings: tensor x data parallel configs. Each tp*dp MUST equal gpu_count. Optional 'ep' (expert-parallel) per-sharding: 'ep':true emits --enable-expert-parallel (shard MoE experts across all ranks); 'ep':false disables it. When 'ep' is omitted, falls back to the model's 'moe' flag — dense models omit it, MoE models get EP on every sharding by default. Sweep ep on/off at the SAME tp/dp to isolate EP's effect on fit + throughput.
_concurrencies: the concurrency sweep — the X-axis that traces the throughput-vs-interactivity Pareto frontier. Matched to the Neuron config (neuron_bench_config.example.json) for the milestone comparison: [1,4,8,16,24,32]. Keep IDENTICAL to the Neuron run. Per-shape overrides via concs_by_shape.
_concs_by_shape: optional per-shape concurrency override keyed 'isl,osl'. The 32768/2048 milestone shape is the KV-cache-pressure regime (KV per seq ~4x the 8k shape), so it fits fewer concurrent requests — capped to [1,4,8,16], byte-matching the Neuron config. Shapes not listed here use the global 'concurrencies'.
_targets: PASS/FAIL latency bars from production (references/profiling-targets.md). ttft_p50_ms_by_isl: TTFT is prefill-bound so the bar scales with input length — keys are ISL thresholds, a cell's bar is the smallest key >= its ISL (short prompts ~500ms, 32K+ ~1.4s). tpot_p50_ms: TPOT is ~input-independent, one bar (~13 ms/tok = ~75 tok/s; fleet sits 9-15). build_deliverables.py flags each usable cell PASS/FAIL vs these (median TTFT/TPOT). Omit this block to skip pass/fail gating.
_workload: dataset = sharegpt|random. DEFAULT: 'sharegpt' — natural-language prompts from ShareGPT-V3. This is the closest thing to production traffic the bench harness has, and it's the correct default because: (a) speculative-decoding acceptance rates depend heavily on prompt distribution (structured/natural text drafts well; random tokens don't), so `random` silently understates any spec-decode regime's value (per the DSpark paper's own results, chat prompts give τ≈3.5 vs random-token acceptance being closer to 1); (b) APC (prefix caching) has near-zero hit rate on random and a real hit rate on shared conversational context; (c) native-production TTFT/TPOT distributions match customer traffic, not synthetic. Use 'random' with 'random_range_ratio 0.0' for the MILESTONE cross-platform GPU-vs-Neuron comparison (EXACTLY-controlled ISL/OSL; Neuron pads to compiled buckets so only exact shapes are comparable — see neuron_bench_config.example.json) — the milestone presets use random+range0. This DIFFERS from this template's sharegpt default, and that is intentional: sharegpt stays the primary for a native-production single-platform study, random+range0 is the correct choice for the matched milestone comparison. num_prompts = max(conc*num_prompts_per_conc, min_prompts) and num_warmups = max(conc*warmups_per_conc, min_warmups) — the FLOORS (50/20) keep even conc=1 at steady state past CUDA-graph capture. Optional 'range_ratio_by_shape' ({"isl,osl": ratio}) overrides the jitter per-shape — use it to set 0.0 on a long shape that would otherwise jitter past the model's context window while keeping 0.8 elsewhere (applies to `random` only). Under sharegpt, seq_len sizes max-model-len and 'shapes' only tags output dirs. max-model-len is sized from the JITTERED isl (isl*(1+ratio)+osl+buffer) under `random`, so a shape's jitter can't overflow its own window — but it still can't exceed the model's native context (use rope_scaling then; see SKILL.md 'Sizing').
_baseline: MILESTONE SERVING-OPTIMIZATION BASELINE (Neuron Agentic Optimization: Performance Milestones, Table 2). The GPU driver (sweep_bench.py) has NO 'baseline' field — controlled vs production is expressed PURELY via the 'server' flags below plus which regimes you include, and it is NOT recorded in regime_meta.json. So a milestone run must encode the baseline in the config's IDENTITY (see 'sweep_name'). TWO baselines, both expressed in THIS template: (1) CONTROLLED (PRIMARY for milestone reporting) = APC OFF + chunked prefill OFF + speculative OFF + DI OFF → server.enable_prefix_caching=false, server.enable_chunked_prefill=false, a single non-spec bf16 regime. (2) PRODUCTION (SECONDARY / GTM) = serving optimizations ON, single instance still (no DI) → server.enable_prefix_caching=true, server.enable_chunked_prefill=true, same single bf16 regime. WHATEVER baseline you run, set the SAME baseline on the Neuron config (neuron_bench_config's 'baseline' field) — the comparison is only valid feature-matched. This generic template leaves server flags at native-production defaults; pick a preset (or set sweep_name + the flags yourself) for a milestone run.
_sweep_name: optional label for this sweep. Read by sweep_bench.py as PREFIX (defaults to the config filename stem) and used for the ledger identity / output-dir naming. RECOMMENDATION for milestones: since regime_meta.json does NOT record the baseline, set sweep_name to encode it (e.g. "llama3_controlled" / "llama3_production") so the milestone tool can recover a GPU run's baseline from the run-dir/ledger name WITHOUT a driver change. Leave null in the generic template.
_server: vllm serve tuning held constant across the sweep. NATIVE-PRODUCTION defaults (E2E config doc): APC (enable_prefix_caching) and chunked prefill ON — what real deployments run; max_num_seqs 256 (vLLM default); max_num_batched_tokens 'auto' = max(2*max_isl, 8192) capped at 16384 (prefill of the largest ISL lands in one scheduler step, identical step size across models). kv_cache_dtype / extra_flags are DEFAULTS a regime can override (regimes[].kv_cache_dtype / .extra_flags). For a strict matched-config run vs a Neuron server lacking chunked prefill, set enable_chunked_prefill false (and see SKILL.md 'Config philosophy').
_fail_threshold: cells whose failed-request fraction exceeds this are SKIPPED (saturation / KV exhaustion is not a clean data point). result.json is still written and synced; the guard only excludes the cell from clean results.
